prompt: A circle has radius $13$ cm. A chord of the circle is $24$ cm long. How far is the chord from the center of the circle, in centimeters?
hint: Draw the perpendicular from the center to the chord — it always cuts the chord exactly in half.

hints.text: Draw the perpendicular from the center to the chord — it always cuts the chord exactly in half.
That makes a right triangle with hypotenuse $13$ (a radius) and one leg $24 \div 2 = 12$.

explanation: A radius drawn perpendicular to a chord bisects that chord, so half the chord is $12$ cm.
Connect the center to an endpoint of the chord: that radius is $13$ cm and forms a right triangle with legs $12$ and $d$.
Solve $12^2 + d^2 = 13^2$: $d^2 = 25$, so the chord sits $5$ cm from the center.

alternativeExplanations.title: The 5-12-13 family again
steps: Half-chord $12$, radius $13$ — that is the $5$-$12$-$13$ triple you met in right triangles.
The missing leg is $5$ with no calculation. Circle problems lean on the Pythagorean theorem constantly, so those triples keep paying off.
